{{Short description|Mathematician}}
'''Nataša Šešum''' is a professor of mathematics at [[Rutgers University]], specializing in [[partial differential equation]]s and [[geometric flow]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.math.rutgers.edu/people/?id=1661|title=Faculty profile: Sesum, Natasa|publisher=Rutgers University, Department of Mathematics|access-date=2015-11-16}}.</ref>

== Education ==
Šešum earned her PhD in 2004 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] under the supervision of [[Gang Tian]]. Her dissertation was ''Limiting Behavior of Ricci Flows''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=84792}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Šešum was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=2015-11-16|archive-date=2017-11-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref>
In 2015 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2015-11-16}}.</ref> She was named [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] Simons Professor for 2015–2016.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-06-07|website=www.msri.org}}</ref> She was awarded the 2023 AMS [[Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics|Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize]] in Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=News from the AMS |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7116 |access-date=2023-04-08 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>
